subproblems.title: A Borel countably n-rectifiable set is, up to a null set, a disjoint union of bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces
subproblems.statement: Let M ⊆ ℝ^P be Borel and countably n-rectifiable. Then there are Lipschitz maps F_i : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^n and constants m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, each F_i(B_i) is a Borel subset of M, the sets F_i(B_i) are pairwise disjoint, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.bilipschitz_pieces-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: step 2 (B1, parametrization) of the supplied proof; used by piece_representation, step 2. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source: step 4 of the parent proof (with the n = 0 provisions of its step 10). It plays the role of Simon's decomposition of Lemma 1.2 / Remark 1.3 of Ch. 3 (chapter-03.txt lines 25–75: M = ⋃_j M_j disjoint, M_j ⊆ N_j, H^n(M_0) = 0), with bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces in place of pieces of C¹ submanifolds; families are indexed by ℕ and empty pieces are allowed. Notation: E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] (on ℝ^n it equals Lebesgue measure, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
1. Rectifiable cover. By CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ ⊆ E with H^n(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → E (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n).
2. Regular sets. Let G_j := {a ∈ ℝ^n : F_j is differentiable at a and DF_j(a) is injective} (SimonGMT areaRegularSet F_j). G_j is Borel (SimonGMT measurableSet_areaRegularSet) and H^n(F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)) = 0 (SimonGMT area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero with s = univ; finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
3. Coercivity constant and radius. For an injective linear A : ℝ^n → E choose m(A) > 0 with (†) |Ah| ≥ m(A)|h| for all h ∈ ℝ^n: if n ≥ 1 take m(A) := min{|Ah| : |h| = 1} (the unit sphere is compact and nonempty and h ↦ |Ah| is continuous and positive on it; for h ≠ 0 apply this to h/|h|; h = 0 is trivial); if n = 0 take m(A) := 1 (the only vector is h = 0). (Alternatively m(A) := 1/K for K > 0 with AntilipschitzWith K A from Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, valid in every dimension.) Define r : (ℝ^n →L[ℝ] E) → ℝ≥0 by r(A) := m(A)/2 if A is injective and r(A) := 1 otherwise. Then r(A) ≠ 0 for every A.
4. Partition. For each j apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := F_j, s := G_j, f' := fderiv ℝ F_j (for a ∈ G_j, F_j is differentiable at a, so HasFDerivWithinAt F_j (DF_j(a)) G_j a) and the radius r of step 3 (rpos holds). It gives pairwise disjoint measurable sets t_{j,k} ⊆ ℝ^n (k ∈ ℕ) with G_j ⊆ ⋃_k t_{j,k}, and continuous linear maps A_{j,k} with ApproximatesLinearOn F_j A_{j,k} (G_j ∩ t_{j,k}) (r(A_{j,k})), i.e. |F_j(a) − F_j(a') − A_{j,k}(a − a')| ≤ r(A_{j,k})|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ G_j ∩ t_{j,k}; and if G_j ≠ ∅ then A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) for some y ∈ G_j.
5. Bi-Lipschitz pieces. Put D_{j,k} := G_j ∩ t_{j,k} (Borel) and ρ_{j,k} := r(A_{j,k}) > 0. Claim: |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ ρ_{j,k}|a − a'| for a, a' ∈ D_{j,k}. If D_{j,k} = ∅ this is vacuous. Otherwise G_j ≠ ∅, so A := A_{j,k} = DF_j(y) with y ∈ G_j is injective and ρ_{j,k} = m(A)/2; by step 4 and (†), |F_j(a) − F_j(a')| ≥ |A(a − a')| − (m(A)/2)|a − a'| ≥ (m(A)/2)|a − a'|. In particular F_j is injective on D_{j,k}, and F_j is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of D_{j,k} ⊆ G_j.
6. Enumeration. Let i ↦ (j(i), k(i)) be the bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ (Nat.unpair). Put F_i := F_{j(i)}, D_i := D_{j(i),k(i)}, m_i := ρ_{j(i),k(i)} > 0, and N_i := F_i(D_i). F_i is continuous, D_i Borel and F_i injective on D_i, so N_i is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
7. Disjoint pieces. Define B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}). B_i is Borel (F_i continuous; M and the N_{i'} Borel) and F_i(B_i) = (N_i ∩ M) ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'} =: P_i, which is Borel and contained in M. Since B_i ⊆ D_i, the lower bound m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| and the differentiability/injectivity of DF_i hold on B_i, and F_i is Lipschitz. If i' < i then P_{i'} ⊆ N_{i'} and P_i ∩ N_{i'} = ∅, so the P_i are pairwise disjoint. (This is the parent's recursive definition B_i := (D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M)) ∖ F_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'})) in closed form: by induction ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(B_{i'}) = M ∩ ⋃_{i'<i} N_{i'}.)
8. Null remainder. Let x ∈ M ∖ (M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j)). By step 1, x = F_j(a) for some j and a, and a ∈ G_j. Then a ∈ t_{j,k} for some k, so a ∈ D_i for the index i with (j(i), k(i)) = (j, k), and x ∈ N_i ∩ M. If i₀ is the least index with x ∈ N_{i₀}, then x ∈ P_{i₀}. Hence M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j), a countable union of H^n-null sets (steps 1–2), so H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0.
9. n = 0 and n > P need no separate treatment: for n = 0 every A is injective, m(A) = 1, r(A) = 1/2, every map ℝ^0 → E is differentiable with injective derivative (G_j = ℝ^0), and each D_i ⊆ ℝ^0 has at most one point; for n > P no linear map ℝ^n → E is injective, so all G_j are empty, all B_i = ∅, and step 8 says H^n(M) = 0. (Imports: areaRegularSet and its lemmas live in Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the frozen statement does not use it.)
proof_key_steps: Cover M by M₀ ∪ ⋃F_j(ℝ^n) and remove the null images F_j(ℝ^n ∖ G_j) of the non-regular points.
Radius r(A) := m(A)/2 for injective A (m(A) a coercivity constant, 1 when n = 0), r(A) := 1 otherwise, so r(A) ≠ 0 for all A.
Mathlib's partition theorem gives pieces G_j ∩ t_{j,k} on which F_j is bi-Lipschitz with lower constant r(A_{j,k}).
Enumerate the pieces over ℕ; their images are Borel by Lusin–Souslin.
B_i := D_i ∩ F_i^{-1}(M ∖ ⋃_{i'<i} F_{i'}(D_{i'})) yields disjoint Borel images in M covering M up to a null set.

Suppose F is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B. Then for Lebesgue-a.e. b ∈ B, F(B) has approximate tangent space range DF(b) at F(b): HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)).

subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.piece_tangent_density-a1.piece_image_tangent-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: step 3 (B2, approximate tangent planes of bi-Lipschitz pieces) of the supplied proof; used by piece_representation, step 4, and by piece_current, step 5. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source: steps 0, 3 (growth bound), 4, 5 and 7 of the parent proof. Here the conclusion is stated for F(B) itself; the comparison with Y in steps 1–3 and 6 is a separate child. Definition used: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S y Q means finrank Q = n and ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} f dH^n → ∫_Q f dH^n as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0) for every f ∈ C_c(E). Notation:
- E := ℝ^P; H^n := μHE[n] on E or on ℝ^n; λ := volume on ℝ^n (= μHE[n] there, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume);
- A := F(B); B̄_r(z) and B_r(z) are the closed and open balls; η_{y,r}(z) := r^{-1}(z − y) (SimonGMT blowUpMap y r);
- J(a) := normDet(DF(a)) (= SimonGMT areaJacobianAt F a); L_b := DF(b); ‖f‖_∞ := sup|f|;
- ω_n := λ(B̄_1(0)) ∈ (0, ∞), so λ(B̄_t(z)) = ω_n t^n for t ≥ 0 (Measure.addHaar_closedBall', finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n).
0. Preliminaries.
(a) F is injective on B: if F(a) = F(a') with a, a' ∈ B then m|a − a'| ≤ 0, and m > 0. F is also continuous. So A is Borel (Lusin–Souslin, MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn; ℝ^n is Polish).
(b) Lipschitz images: H^n(F(S)) ≤ L^n H^n(S) = L^n λ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n (SimonGMT euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).
(c) Growth: let b ∈ B and s > 0. If a ∈ B and F(a) ∈ B̄_s(F(b)), then m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| ≤ s. So A ∩ B̄_s(F(b)) ⊆ F(B̄_{s/m}(b)), and by (b), H^n(A ∩ B̄_s(F(b))) ≤ L^n ω_n m^{-n} s^n.
(d) Scaling: let r > 0. η_{y,r} is the homothety with centre y and ratio r^{-1} followed by the translation z ↦ z − y. So H^n(η_{y,r}(S)) = r^{-n} H^n(S) for every S ⊆ E (MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image, Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
- η_{y,r} is a homeomorphism (inverse w ↦ y + rw), hence a measurable embedding that maps Borel sets to Borel sets, and |η_{y,r}(z)| < R ⇔ |z − y| < rR.
- For Borel S, the image of H^n⌞S under η_{y,r} is r^n·H^n⌞η_{y,r}(S): for Borel T, H^n(S ∩ η_{y,r}^{-1}(T)) = r^n H^n(η_{y,r}(S) ∩ T).
- In Lean form: Measure.map η_{y,r} (μHE[n].restrict S) = ENNReal.ofReal (r^n) • μHE[n].restrict (η_{y,r} '' S). Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(S)} g dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_S g(η_{y,r}(z)) dH^n(z) for every Borel g : E → ℝ (MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map, integral_smul_measure). No integrability is needed: if one side is not integrable, neither is the other, and both integrals are 0.
(e) Jacobian: J is Borel (SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and 0 ≤ J(a) ≤ L^n for every a.
- ‖DF(a)‖ ≤ L by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; DF(a) = 0 where F is not differentiable.
- For every linear T : ℝ^n → E, normDet(T)·ω_n = H^n(T(B̄_1(0))) ≤ ‖T‖^n ω_n. The equality is LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume. The inequality is euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn for the ‖T‖-Lipschitz map T (T.lipschitz), together with μHE[n] = λ on ℝ^n.
- Since ω_n ∈ (0, ∞), normDet(T) ≤ ‖T‖^n.
(f) Area formula: ∫⁻_A g dH^n = ∫⁻_B J(a) g(F(a)) dλ(a) for every g : E → [0, ∞]. This is SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn with s = B, using (a) and finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n.
1. Good parameters. Two theorems apply to λ:
- the Lebesgue density theorem (Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for λ and B);
- the Lebesgue differentiation theorem, applied to J, which is bounded and Borel, hence locally integrable. Use IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub with μ := volume (doubling by the instance isUnifLocDoublingMeasureOfIsAddHaarMeasure), K := 1, ι := ℝ, l := 𝓝[>] 0, w := fun _ ↦ b and δ := id; the side condition b ∈ B̄_ρ(b) is trivial, and the radii tend to 0⁺ by self_mem_nhdsWithin.
So λ-a.e. b ∈ B satisfies:
(α) λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺. Since λ(B̄_ρ(b)) = ω_n ρ^n ∈ (0, ∞), equivalently ρ^{-n} λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B) → 0.
(β) ⨍_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) → 0 as ρ → 0⁺, equivalently ρ^{-n} ∫_{B̄_ρ(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) → 0.
The set of b ∈ B satisfying (α) and (β) is (volume.restrict B)-conull and does not depend on any test function. Fix such b. F is differentiable at b by hypothesis. Put y := F(b) and L_b := DF(b).
2. Lower bound (γ): m|c| ≤ |L_b c| for every c ∈ ℝ^n.
- This is trivial for c = 0. Let c ≠ 0, so n ≥ 1 and ℝ^n is nontrivial, and let δ ∈ (0, |c|).
- For r > 0 the open ball W_r := B_{rδ}(b + rc) satisfies W_r ⊆ B̄_{r(|c|+δ)}(b) and λ(W_r) = ω_n (rδ)^n (open and closed balls have equal measure, Measure.addHaar_closedBall_eq_addHaar_ball).
- If W_r ∩ B = ∅, then with ρ := r(|c| + δ), λ(B̄_ρ(b) ∖ B)/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) ≥ (δ/(|c| + δ))^n > 0. By (α) this ratio tends to 0, so there is r_δ > 0 with W_r ∩ B ≠ ∅ for all r ∈ (0, r_δ).
- Let θ > 0. Differentiability at b gives ρ_θ > 0 with |F(b + h) − F(b) − L_b h| ≤ θ|h| whenever |h| < ρ_θ.
- Choose r ∈ (0, r_δ) with r(|c| + δ) < ρ_θ, and c' with |c' − c| < δ and b + rc' ∈ B. Since b and b + rc' lie in B, m r|c'| ≤ |F(b + rc') − F(b)| ≤ r|L_b c'| + θ r|c'|. So m|c'| ≤ |L_b c'| + θ|c'|.
- Using |c| − δ ≤ |c'| ≤ |c| + δ and |L_b c'| ≤ |L_b c| + ‖L_b‖δ gives m(|c| − δ) ≤ |L_b c| + ‖L_b‖δ + θ(|c| + δ).
- This holds for every θ > 0 and δ ∈ (0, |c|). Letting θ → 0 and then δ → 0 gives m|c| ≤ |L_b c|.
Consequently L_b is injective and finrank(range L_b) = n (LinearMap.finrank_range_of_inj).
3. Setup. Fix f ∈ C_c(E). Choose R > 0 with f(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ R (tsupport f is compact, hence bounded). Let M := ‖f‖_∞ < ∞ and D := B̄_{R/m}(0) ⊆ ℝ^n. For r > 0 and c ∈ ℝ^n let Φ_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − F(b))/r.
4. Rescaled area formula. For every r > 0, f is H^n-integrable on η_{y,r}(A) and
∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c).
(i) η_{y,r}(A) is Borel. Also η_{y,r}(A) ∩ B_R(0) = η_{y,r}(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)), which has H^n-measure r^{-n} H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)) ≤ L^n ω_n (R/m)^n < ∞ by 0(c) and 0(d). Since f is Borel, |f| ≤ M and f = 0 off B_R(0), f is integrable on η_{y,r}(A).
(ii) By 0(d), ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n = r^{-n} ∫_A g dH^n with g := f∘η_{y,r}. g is Borel, |g| ≤ M and g = 0 off B_{rR}(y).
(iii) Apply 0(f) to the weights g⁺ := max(g, 0), g⁻ := max(−g, 0) and |g|.
- ∫⁻_A g^± dH^n = ∫⁻_B J(a) g^±(F(a)) dλ(a), and ∫⁻_B J(a)|g(F(a))| dλ(a) = ∫⁻_A |g| dH^n ≤ M H^n(A ∩ B_{rR}(y)) < ∞.
- So a ↦ 1_B(a) J(a) g(F(a)) is Borel and λ-integrable. As J ≥ 0, its positive and negative parts are a ↦ 1_B(a) J(a) g^±(F(a)).
- Write both Bochner integrals as differences of the lintegrals of their positive and negative parts (integral_eq_lintegral_pos_part_sub_lintegral_neg_part). This gives ∫_A g dH^n = ∫_B J(a) g(F(a)) dλ(a).
(iv) Substitute a = b + rc. λ is translation invariant and ∫ h(rc) dλ(c) = r^{-n} ∫ h dλ for r > 0 (Measure.integral_comp_smul). Using (F(b + rc) − y)/r = Φ_r(c), this gives ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(a) J(a) f((F(a) − y)/r) dλ(a) = r^n ∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c). Combining (ii)–(iv) proves the formula.
5. Localisation.
- If b + rc ∈ B and f(Φ_r(c)) ≠ 0, then |Φ_r(c)| < R. So m r|c| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)| < rR, and |c| < R/m.
- If f(L_b c) ≠ 0 then |L_b c| < R, and by (γ), |c| < R/m.
Hence the integrand of step 4 and c ↦ J(b) f(L_b c) both vanish outside D, and I_∞ := ∫_{ℝ^n} J(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c) = ∫_D J(b) f(L_b c) dλ(c).
6. Convergence: ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n → I_∞ as r → 0⁺.
- Let c ∈ D. Add and subtract J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) and J(b) f(Φ_r(c)), and use 0 ≤ J ≤ L^n and |f| ≤ M:
|1_B(b + rc) J(b + rc) f(Φ_r(c)) − J(b) f(L_b c)| ≤ L^n M 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) + M|J(b + rc) − J(b)| + J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)|.
- All three terms are bounded Borel functions of c, D has finite measure ω_n (R/m)^n, and both integrands vanish off D by step 5. So |∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n − I_∞| is at most the integral over D of the right-hand side.
(i) ∫_D 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) dλ(c) = r^{-n} λ(B̄_{rR/m}(b) ∖ B) = (R/m)^n · s^{-n} λ(B̄_s(b) ∖ B) with s := rR/m → 0⁺. This tends to 0 by (α).
(ii) ∫_D |J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) = r^{-n} ∫_{B̄_{rR/m}(b)} |J(a) − J(b)| dλ(a) = (R/m)^n · s^{-n} ∫_{B̄_s(b)} |J − J(b)| dλ. This tends to 0 by (β).
(iii) Given θ > 0, let ρ_θ be as in step 2. For 0 < r < ρ_θ m/R and c ∈ D we have |rc| < ρ_θ, so |Φ_r(c) − L_b c| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b) − L_b(rc)| ≤ θ|c| ≤ θR/m. Thus Φ_r → L_b uniformly on D. Since f is uniformly continuous (CompactlySupportedContinuousMapClass.uniformContinuous), sup_{c ∈ D} |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| → 0. Hence ∫_D J(b)|f(Φ_r(c)) − f(L_b c)| dλ(c) ≤ J(b) λ(D) sup_D |…| → 0.
Hence ∫_{η_{y,r}(A)} f dH^n → I_∞.
7. Identification: I_∞ = ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n.
- By LinearMap.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_eq_normDet_mul_volume (finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n), H^n(L_b(S)) = normDet(L_b) λ(S) = J(b) λ(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^n.
- For Borel T ⊆ E, L_b(L_b^{-1}(T)) = range L_b ∩ T, so H^n(range L_b ∩ T) = J(b) λ(L_b^{-1}(T)). That is, H^n⌞range L_b is the image measure of J(b)·λ under L_b (range L_b is closed, hence Borel).
- L_b is an injective linear map between finite-dimensional spaces, hence a closed embedding (LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective) and a measurable embedding. So MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and integral_smul_measure give ∫_{range L_b} f dH^n = J(b) ∫_{ℝ^n} f(L_b c) dλ(c) = I_∞.
8. Conclusion. By steps 4, 6 and 7, ∫_{η_{F(b),r}(F(B))} f dH^n → ∫_{range DF(b)} f dH^n as r → 0⁺ for every f ∈ C_c(E), and finrank(range DF(b)) = n by step 2. So HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (range DF(b)) holds at every b ∈ B satisfying (α) and (β), that is, for (volume.restrict B)-a.e. b.
9. Dimension zero. For n = 0 the argument runs as written:
- ℝ^0 = {0} = D, B ⊆ {0}, ω_0 ∈ (0, ∞) and r^{±0} = 1;
- J ≡ 1 (LinearMap.normDet_of_subsingleton);
- (α) and (β) hold at b = 0 when 0 ∈ B, and (γ) concerns only c = 0;
- range L_b = {0} has finrank 0.
(Optional observation, not used: if n > P, no injective DF(a) exists, so B = ∅. Steps 0–8 need no case split, since (γ) already yields injectivity at good points.)

subproblems.title: Injective area formula with the Gram-determinant Jacobian, and Borel measurability of that Jacobian
subproblems.statement: Let m, P ∈ ℕ and f : ℝ^m → ℝ^P. Let Df(x) := fderiv ℝ f x (the zero map where f is not differentiable), e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1, and Jf(x) := (det[⟨Df(x)e_k, Df(x)e_l⟩]_{k,l})^{1/2} (Real.sqrt). Then (i) Jf : ℝ^m → ℝ is Borel measurable; (ii) for every Borel s ⊆ ℝ^m such that f is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective and f is injective on s, and for every g : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x), where H^m := μHE[m] on ℝ^P and λ := volume is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m P : ℕ) (f : Euclid m → Euclid P), Measurable (fun x => Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) ∧ ∀ s : Set (Euclid m), MeasurableSet s → (∀ x ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) → (∀ x ∈ s, Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)) → InjOn f s → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in f '' s, g y ∂μHE[m] = ∫⁻ x in s, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun k l : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single k 1)) (fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single l 1))))) * g (f x) ∂volume
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.codim1_lura_gram_area_formula (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.local_unit_rep-a1.area_formula-a1.gram_area-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the injective area formula with the Gram-determinant Jacobian (lintegral form, with Borel measurability of the Jacobian) cited throughout the supplied proof; used by piece_representation, steps 6, 8 and 9, and by piece_current, step 5. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source: the Notation paragraph of the parent proof (normDet Λ := (det[⟨Λe_k, Λe_l⟩])^{1/2} and SimonGMT areaJacobianAt f a = normDet Df(a)), its step 4 (measurability of b ↦ normDet D(·)(b) via SimonGMT measurable_areaJacobianAt) and its step 6(a) (the injective area formula SimonGMT weighted_area_formula_of_injective_derivative with finrank ℝ^m = m and an arbitrary weight), isolated for a single map f. Notation: e_k := EuclideanSpace.single k 1; (e_k)_{k<m} is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^m (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.basisFun, whose k-th vector is EuclideanSpace.single k 1 by EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply). For a linear map T : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, normDet T ≥ 0 is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet, and SimonGMT defines areaJacobianAt f x := normDet(Df(x)) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet).

1. (Jf = areaJacobianAt f.) Let x ∈ ℝ^m and T := Df(x). Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, applied to T and the orthonormal basis (e_k) of ℝ^m, gives normDet(T)² = det Gram(Te_0, …, Te_{m−1}), where Gram(v) = Matrix.gram ℝ v = Matrix.of (k, l ↦ ⟨v_k, v_l⟩) and the coercion ℝ → ℝ is the identity. So normDet(T)² = det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩]. As normDet(T) ≥ 0, normDet(T) = (normDet(T)²)^{1/2} = (det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩])^{1/2}. Hence Jf(x) = normDet(Df(x)) = areaJacobianAt f x for every x ∈ ℝ^m (not only on s).

2. (Proof of (i).) SimonGMT Chapter02 measurable_areaJacobianAt states that x ↦ areaJacobianAt f x is measurable for every f between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces. By step 1 the functions Jf and areaJacobianAt f are equal, so Jf is Borel measurable. (Alternatively: Df is Borel by Mathlib measurable_fderiv, and T ↦ (det[⟨Te_k, Te_l⟩])^{1/2} is continuous on the space of linear maps, as a composition of evaluations, inner products, a polynomial determinant and the square root.)

3. (The injective area formula.) SimonGMT Chapter02 weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative (Simon (3.5) for an injective regular parametrization in arbitrary codimension) states: if E, F are finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with their Borel σ-algebras, s ⊆ E is Borel, f : E → F is differentiable at every x ∈ s with Df(x) injective, f is injective on s, and g : F → [0, ∞] is arbitrary, then ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) · g(f(x)) dλ_E(x), with λ_E = volume on E. Apply it with E := ℝ^m, F := ℝ^P and the given s, f, g. Since finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), the measure on the left is μHE[m] = H^m.

4. (Proof of (ii).) By step 1 the integrands ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) · g(f(x)) and ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) agree at every x, so the right side of step 3 equals ∫⁻_s ofReal(Jf(x)) · g(f(x)) dλ(x). This is (ii). ∎

Lean remark: the proof uses SimonGMT's Chapter02 area modules; Submission.lean may add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea` (which also brings Mathlib's NormDet). The statement itself needs no extra import.
proof_key_steps: normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.single k 1 gives Jf(x) = normDet Df(x) = areaJacobianAt f x for every x.
measurable_areaJacobianAt gives Borel measurability of Jf: conclusion (i).
SimonGMT's weighted injective area formula with finrank ℝ^m = m gives ∫⁻_{f(s)} g dH^m = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt f x) g(f x) dλ for arbitrary g.
Replacing areaJacobianAt f by Jf pointwise gives conclusion (ii).

subproblems.title: Injective-immersion area formula on a Borel subset of ℝ^m with Gram-determinant Jacobian
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let G : ℝ^m → ℝ^P, and let F ⊆ ℝ^m be a Borel set. Assume G is differentiable at every v ∈ F with injective derivative DG(v), and G is injective on F. Let e_0, …, e_{m−1} be the standard basis of ℝ^m.

Then for every function h : ℝ^P → ℝ:
∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j<m})^{1/2} · h(G(v)) dL^m(v).

Here H^m = μHE[m] is the normalized m-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^P and L^m is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^m. Both sides are Bochner integrals; no integrability is assumed, and a non-integrable integral is 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (G : Euclid m → Euclid P) (F : Set (Euclid m)), MeasurableSet F → (∀ v ∈ F, DifferentiableAt ℝ G v) → (∀ v ∈ F, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G v)) → InjOn G F → ∀ h : Euclid P → ℝ, ∫ w in G '' F, h w ∂μHE[m] = ∫ v in F, Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin m => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single i 1)) (fderiv ℝ G v (EuclideanSpace.single j 1)))) * h (G v)
subproblems.natural_proof:
This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram (DAG node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.region_density_one-a1.local_unit_rep-a1.chart_divergence-a1.gram_area_formula-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the injective area formula in Bochner-integral form cited throughout the supplied proof; used by piece_representation, step 11, and by piece_current, step 6. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source. Step 9 ((1b), area formula) of the parent's supplied proof of codim1_lur_chart_divergence_formula, stated for an arbitrary dimension m, map G and Borel set F (Simon Ch. 2, (3.3)–(3.5)).

Implementation note: the proof uses SimonGMT's Chapter02 area formula, so GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean must add `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.WeightedArea`. There is precedent: accepted solution commit c2cf4bd9 added `import Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz`. The statement itself only uses notions already imported.

1. (SimonGMT area formula.) Apply SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean) with:
- source space E = ℝ^m and target ℝ^P;
- s = F (measurable);
- f = G, which is differentiable at every point of F with injective derivative and injective on F;
- integrand h.
It gives ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[finrank ℝ^m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v • h(G(v)) dμHE[finrank ℝ^m](v). This identity holds for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ without integrability hypotheses. It is derived from the measure identity map(G|_F)(J·μHE⌞F) = μHE⌞G(F) via MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map and setIntegral_withDensity_eq_setIntegral_smul₀.

2. (Normalize the measures.) finrank ℝ ℝ^m = m (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). On ℝ^m, μHE[finrank ℝ^m] equals Lebesgue measure (InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE[m] = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G(v)) dv.

3. (Gram form of the Jacobian.) Fix v ∈ F and put L := DG(v).
- By definition areaJacobianAt G v = normDet(L) (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), and normDet(L) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg).
- Apply Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram to the linear map L and the standard orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun of ℝ^m, whose vectors are e_i. It gives normDet(L)² = det Gram(Le_0, …, Le_{m−1}), where Matrix.gram ℝ w i j = ⟨w_i, w_j⟩; that is, normDet(L)² = det[⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩]_{i,j}.
- Taking the nonnegative square root (Real.sqrt_sq): areaJacobianAt G v = (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩]_{i,j})^{1/2}.
(Equivalently: normDet(L)² = det(L*L), and the matrix of L*L in the orthonormal basis (e_i) has entries ⟨e_i, L*Le_j⟩ = ⟨Le_i, Le_j⟩.)

4. (Conclusion.) Substitute step 3 into the right side of step 2 pointwise on the measurable set F (setIntegral_congr_fun; the scalar action is real multiplication). This gives ∫_{G(F)} h dH^m = ∫_F (det[⟨DG(v)e_i, DG(v)e_j⟩])^{1/2} h(G(v)) dv. ∎
proof_key_steps: SimonGMT integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative: ∫_{G(F)} h dμHE = ∫_F areaJacobianAt G v · h(G v) dμHE for every h, with no integrability hypothesis.
On ℝ^m, finrank = m and μHE[m] = volume.
areaJacobianAt G v = normDet DG(v) = (det Gram(DG(v)e_i))^{1/2}, by normDet_sq_eq_det_gram with the standard orthonormal basis and normDet ≥ 0; then setIntegral_congr_fun on F.

subproblems.title: An integer-valued density on an oriented rectifiable set gives an IMRep
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. Let N ⊆ U be Borel and countably n-rectifiable with Hⁿ(N ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Let η : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n) be strongly measurable. Let m : ℝ^P → ℝ be measurable with m(x) ∈ ℤ for every x and ∫_{N∩K} |m| dHⁿ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U. Assume that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ N there is a linear subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η(x)) Q. Then there is an IMRep R in U such that R.action(ω) = ∫_N m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)) dHⁿ(x) for every n-form ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n, no regularity required).

This is the comparator-accepted theorem Submission.cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density (DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.deformation_theorem-a1.im_series-a1.density_imrep-a1), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; it needs no new proof work. Role in this decomposition: the IMRep built from an integer density and an orientation in step 5(b) of the supplied proof; used by piece_current, step 5. Its step 5 uses the accepted theorem Submission.rsdic_ae_tangent_iff_of_subset, called the sibling tangent_locality in its original decomposition; that theorem is part of the accepted history of this node, so no sibling dependency is needed here. The proof below is the one formalized there.

Source: steps (5e) and (5g) of the supplied proof: the IMRep (N', |m|, sign(m)η) built from an integer multiplicity m and an orientation η of N. Tangent planes pass from N to N' by locality, which is (IMC)(a), here the reused sibling tangent_locality. Stated for an arbitrary open U and degree n; the supplied proof's removal of a null set Z is unnecessary because the IMRep fields are a.e. conditions.

Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n].

1. (Carrier.) N' := N ∩ {x : m(x) ≠ 0}. It is Borel: N is Borel and m is measurable, so {m ≠ 0} = m⁻¹(ℝ ∖ {0}) is Borel. Also N' ⊆ N ⊆ U.
2. (Multiplicity.) mult(x) := ⌊|m(x)|⌋₊ ∈ ℕ (Nat.floor). For every x, m(x) = z for some z ∈ ℤ, and |m(x)| = |z| is the natural number natAbs z, so (mult(x) : ℝ) = |m(x)|. mult is measurable as the composition of the measurable m, the continuous |·| and the monotone, hence measurable, ⌊·⌋₊ : ℝ → ℕ (Monotone.measurable). For x ∈ N', m(x) ≠ 0, so mult(x) = |m(x)| > 0.
3. (Orientation.) orient(x) := −η(x) if m(x) < 0, and orient(x) := η(x) otherwise. It is strongly measurable: η and −η = (−1)•η are strongly measurable, {m < 0} is Borel, and the piecewise combination is strongly measurable (StronglyMeasurable.ite). In particular orient is a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞N'.
4. (Rectifiability, local integrability.) N' ⊆ N, so N' is countably n-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono). For compact K ⊆ U: ∫_{N'∩K} mult dμ ≤ ∫_{N∩K} mult dμ = ∫_{N∩K} |m| dμ < ∞, by monotonicity in the set, step 2 and the hypothesis.
5. (Orientation field.) Apply sibling tangent_locality with open U, small set N' and large set N. Here N' ⊆ N ⊆ U are Borel and N is locally finite by hypothesis. So for μ⌞N'-a.e. x and every Q: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q. The hypothesis on η holds μ⌞N-a.e., hence μ⌞N'-a.e., since N' ⊆ N. Take x outside both exceptional null sets and Q from the hypothesis. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N' x Q, and orient(x) ∈ {η(x), −η(x)} is a unit orientation of Q. Indeed, if η(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α (resp. −α(τ)), with τ orthonormal spanning Q, then −η(x)(α) = −α(τ) (resp. α(τ)); IsUnitOrientationOf allows either sign with the same τ.
6. Steps 1–5 verify every field of IMRep (measurableSet_carrier, carrier_subset, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, locallyIntegrable_mult, aestronglyMeasurable_orient, orients). So R := (N', mult, orient) is an IMRep in U.
7. (Action.) Let ω be any n-form. For x ∈ N:
   - if m(x) = 0, then x ∉ N' and 1_{N'}(x)·mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = 0 = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x));
   - if m(x) ≠ 0, then x ∈ N' and mult(x)·orient(x)(ω(x)) = |m(x)|·(±η(x)(ω(x))) = m(x)·η(x)(ω(x)), the sign being that of m(x).
   So the functions 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) and m·η(ω) agree at every point of N. Hence R.action(ω) = ∫_{N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ = ∫_{N ∩ N'} mult·orient(ω) dμ (since N ∩ N' = N') = ∫_N 1_{N'}·mult·orient(ω) dμ (setIntegral_indicator) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dμ (setIntegral_congr_fun). No integrability is needed: Bochner integrals over N of functions that agree pointwise on N coincide. ∎

N' ⊆ N gives rectifiability; ∫_{N'∩K} |m| ≤ ∫_{N∩K} |m| < ∞ gives local integrability.
tangent_locality for N' ⊆ N moves the oriented approximate tangent planes of N to N'; ±η(x) is still a unit orientation.
1_{N'}·|m|·sign(m)η(ω) = m·η(ω) pointwise on N, so R.action(ω) = ∫_N m·η(ω) dHⁿ for every form ω.

subproblems.title: Unit orientation of the span of independent vectors and the Gram-Jacobian identity (Simon 6.3.4–3.5; supplied (0a)–(0b))
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every linearly independent family v = (v_0, …, v_{n−1}) in ℝ^P (Euclid P), let G := (⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} be its Gram matrix and J := √det G. Then: (i) det G > 0; (ii) J ≤ ∏_a |v_a|; (iii) there is ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) that is a unit orientation of V := span{v_a} (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ V) and satisfies α(v_0, …, v_{n−1}) = J·ξ(α) for every n-covector α; (iv) every unit orientation ζ of V equals ξ or −ξ.

Source: steps (0a)–(0b) of the supplied proof (orthonormal frame of the span, “α(Ae) = JA·α(τ)”, and “two orthonormal bases of the same n-plane give α(τ') = ±α(τ) with a sign independent of α”); this is Simon Ch. 6, 3.4–3.5 (D₁f ∧ ⋯ ∧ Dₙf = det(Dᵢf·τⱼ)·τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ and J = |det(Dᵢf·τⱼ)|), isolated for one linearly independent family.

Notation. V := span{v_0, …, v_{n−1}} ⊆ ℝ^P (Lean: Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v)); G := (⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b} is the Gram matrix and J := √det G. An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map ℝ^P → ℝ, and α(z) is its value at a family z : Fin n → ℝ^P. For such z, ev_z is the functional α ↦ α(z). It is linear in α and satisfies |α(z)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_a|z_a| (operator norm), so it is a continuous linear functional, i.e. an element of MultiVector P n (LinearMap.mkContinuous; Covector (Euclid P) n is in any case finite-dimensional).

1. (Orthonormal frame.) v is linearly independent, so it is a basis of V and dim V = n. Let σ := gramSchmidtNormed ℝ v (Mathlib InnerProductSpace.gramSchmidtNormed). By gramSchmidtNormed_orthonormal, σ is orthonormal. By the Gram–Schmidt construction, span{σ_0, …, σ_b} = span{v_0, …, v_b} for every b. In particular span(range σ) = V, so σ is an orthonormal basis of V. [Optional, not used below: if this node is decomposed further, the accepted theorem dpf_exists_orthonormal_frame_det_gram (an orthonormal σ with span σ = span v, det G = (det A)², det A ≠ 0 and |det A| ≤ ∏_a|v_a|) can be reused as a child with its identical frozen type to shorten steps 1–4. Without such a decomposition it is not available, and the self-contained argument here applies.]
2. (Coordinates.) Put A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ for a, b ∈ Fin n. Since v_b ∈ V and σ is an orthonormal basis of V, v_b = Σ_a A_{ab}σ_a. A is upper triangular. Indeed, for a > b we have v_b ∈ span{σ_0, …, σ_b}, and this span is orthogonal to σ_a, so A_{ab} = 0.
3. ((i).) Expanding with step 2 and orthonormality, ⟨v_a, v_b⟩ = Σ_{c,d} A_{ca}A_{db}⟨σ_c, σ_d⟩ = Σ_c A_{ca}A_{cb}. So G = AᵀA and det G = (det A)². The columns of A are the σ-coordinate vectors of the linearly independent vectors v_b, so A is invertible and det A ≠ 0. Hence det G = (det A)² > 0, which is (i), and J = √((det A)²) = |det A| > 0.
4. ((ii), Hadamard.) A is upper triangular, so det A = ∏_b A_{bb} (Matrix.det_of_isUpperTriangular). By Cauchy–Schwarz, |A_{bb}| = |⟨σ_b, v_b⟩| ≤ |σ_b|·|v_b| = |v_b|. Hence J = |det A| ≤ ∏_b |v_b|.
5. (Expansion.) For every n-covector α, α(v) = det(A)·α(σ). Indeed, let α_V be the alternating n-linear form (w_0, …, w_{n−1}) ↦ α(w_0, …, w_{n−1}) on V. Since dim V = n, every alternating n-form on V is a multiple of the determinant det_σ relative to the basis σ: α_V = α_V(σ)·det_σ (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at v gives α(v) = α(σ)·det_σ(v). The number det_σ(v) is the determinant of the matrix whose (a, b) entry is the a-th σ-coordinate of v_b, namely ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩ = A_{ab}; so det_σ(v) = det A. Alternatively, by multilinearity α(v) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin n} (∏_b A_{f(b) b})·α(σ∘f). Terms with non-injective f vanish by alternation, and α(σ∘π) = sign(π)·α(σ) for permutations π; the Leibniz formula then gives det(A)·α(σ).
6. (Definition of ξ; (iii).) Let ε := sign(det A) ∈ {1, −1} (det A ≠ 0) and ξ := ε·ev_σ ∈ MultiVector P n, i.e. ξ(α) = ε·α(σ). By step 5, for every α, α(v) = det(A)·α(σ) = |det A|·ε·α(σ) = J·ξ(α). σ is orthonormal with span(range σ) = V. Either ξ(α) = α(σ) for all α (ε = 1) or ξ(α) = −α(σ) for all α (ε = −1). This is IsUnitOrientationOf ξ V, witnessed by τ := σ.
7. ((iv), uniqueness.) Let ζ be a unit orientation of V. Then there are an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = V and δ ∈ {1, −1} with ζ(α) = δ·α(τ) for all α. The τ_b are n orthonormal vectors in the n-dimensional space V, so they form an orthonormal basis of V. Put O_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, τ_b⟩. Steps 2, 3 and 5 with τ in place of v give: τ_b = Σ_a O_{ab}σ_a; OᵀO = (⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩)_{a,b} = I, so det O ∈ {1, −1}; and α(τ) = det(O)·α(σ) for every α. Hence ζ(α) = δ·det(O)·α(σ) = (δ·det(O)·ε)·ξ(α) for every α (ε² = 1). The constant δ·det(O)·ε ∈ {1, −1} does not depend on α. Therefore ζ = ξ or ζ = −ξ (continuous linear maps that agree on every α are equal). [Optional, not used: if this node is decomposed further, (iv) also follows from (iii) by the accepted theorem rsdic_unitOrientation_eq_or_eq_neg, reused as a child with its identical frozen type.]
8. (n = 0.) The argument covers this case with empty families. V = {0}; G and A are 0×0 matrices with determinant 1, so det G = 1 > 0 and J = 1 = ∏_∅. α(v) = α(σ), both being the value at the empty family. ξ = ev_∅, and every unit orientation of {0} is ±ev_∅ (step 7 with det O = 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose the Gram–Schmidt orthonormal basis σ of V = span v and put A_{ab} := ⟨σ_a, v_b⟩, so that v_b = Σ_a A_{ab}σ_a and A is upper triangular.
G = AᵀA, so det G = (det A)² > 0 by independence, and |det A| = ∏|⟨σ_b, v_b⟩| ≤ ∏|v_b| (Hadamard).
α(v) = det(A)·α(σ), since alternating n-forms on V are multiples of det_σ.
ξ := sign(det A)·(α ↦ α(σ)) is a unit orientation of V with α(v) = J·ξ(α).
Two orthonormal bases of V differ by an orthogonal matrix, so every unit orientation of V is ±ξ.

Source: step 1 (normalization), step 2 (B1, parametrization), step 3 (B2, B2′: tangent planes and sign of the pieces) of the supplied proof, and the area-formula representation X(η) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i η(G_i)(DG_i e) used in its steps 4 and 7. This is Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.5: the decomposition of T = τ(M, θ, ξ) into Lipschitz pieces and the identity d f_# ξ = ±J ξ̃.

Hypotheses as named in the statement:
- (CB) is the frozen type of cmcdt_lp_covector_norm_bounds; its third conjunct (L3) says |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ.
- (VO), (MR), (IMC) are the frozen types of dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure and cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub.

Notation:
- n := k + 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; λ := volume on ℝⁿ = Euclid n.
- e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 (a ∈ Fin n), the standard basis of ℝⁿ; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
- For G : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N and u ∈ ℝⁿ: DG(u) := fderiv ℝ G u; v^G(u) := (DG(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin n}; J_G(u) := √det(⟨DG(u)e_a, DG(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b} ≥ 0. This is exactly the Jacobian in the siblings area_lintegral and area_integral.
- ev_z is the evaluation functional α ↦ α(z) on n-covectors. It is continuous linear, and z ↦ ev_z is continuous.
- For a test form η, ‖η‖_∞ := sup_x |η(x)| < ∞, since η is continuous with compact support and α ↦ |α| is continuous.

1. (Normalization.) Let R be an IMRep representing X, with carrier M₀, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. spt X is closed, hence Borel. (IMC)(b) with U := ℝ^N and E := spt X gives a current A and an IMRep R' representing A, with carrier M := M₀ ∩ spt X, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ.
   Put W := ℝ^N ∖ spt X; it is open. Every ω admissible for massOn W (tsupport ω ⊆ W, |ω(x)| ≤ 1) has tsupport disjoint from spt X, so X(ω) = 0 by (VO). Hence X.massOn W = sSup{ofReal 0} = 0.
   By (MR) for (X, R): 0 = X.massOn W = R.measure W = ∫⁻_{M₀ ∩ W} θ dHⁿ. Since θ ≥ 1 on M₀, Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ spt X) = Hⁿ(M₀ ∩ W) = 0.
   Therefore Hⁿ⌞M = Hⁿ⌞M₀, and for every test form η, R'.action(η) = ∫_M θ ξ(η) dHⁿ = ∫_{M₀} θ ξ(η) dHⁿ = R.action(η) = X(η). So R' represents X. Consequences:
   (a) By (MR) for (X, R') with W := ℝ^N: X.mass = X.massOn ℝ^N = R'.measure(ℝ^N) = ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ < ∞.
   (b) Hⁿ(M) ≤ ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ < ∞, because θ ≥ 1 on M.
   (c) By (IMC)(d) for R': for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every α.
   (d) M ⊆ spt X. By the IMRep fields of R', M is Borel and countably n-rectifiable, and for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is Q_x with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q_x and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q_x.
2. (Pieces, B1.) Apply the sibling bilipschitz_pieces (dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces, with P := N) to the Borel, countably n-rectifiable set M. It gives, for i ∈ ℕ, maps G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N with Lipschitz constants L_i, Borel sets A_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and numbers m_i > 0 such that:
   - m_i|u − u'| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(u')| for u, u' ∈ A_i;
   - G_i is differentiable at every u ∈ A_i, with DG_i(u) injective;
   - the sets G_i(A_i) are Borel, contained in M and pairwise disjoint;
   - Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0.
   This gives the Lipschitz, Borel and differentiability conclusions, and G_i(A_i) ⊆ M ⊆ spt X. G_i is injective on A_i.
3. (Null sets pull back.) Fix i. For every E ⊆ A_i, λ(E) ≤ m_i^{-n}·Hⁿ(G_i(E)). Indeed, the inverse of G_i on G_i(E) is m_i^{-1}-Lipschitz. Lipschitz maps multiply Hⁿ by at most the n-th power of their constant (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le; μHE[n] is a constant multiple of μH[n]). And Hⁿ = λ on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). [Optional, not used: if this node is decomposed further, this bound is the lower bound in the accepted theorem dimred_rpd_bilipschitz_image_measure, which can then be reused as a child with its identical frozen type.]
   Consequently, if a property p holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, then p(G_i(u)) holds for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i. To see this, apply the bound to E := A_i ∩ G_i^{-1}(Z), where Z is the exceptional set: Hⁿ(Z ∩ M) = 0 and G_i(E) ⊆ Z ∩ M. The same holds for Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i)-a.e. properties.
4. (Tangent planes, B2.) Fix i. The sibling piece_tangent (ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae with F := G_i, B := A_i, L := L_i, m := m_i) gives: for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, G_i(A_i) has approximate tangent space range DG_i(u) at G_i(u).
   Apply (IMC)(a) with U := ℝ^N, the Borel sets G_i(A_i) ⊆ M, and the bound Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M) < ∞. For Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i)-a.e. x and every Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (G_i(A_i)) x Q ⟺ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q.
   By step 3, this equivalence, the orientation property 1(d) and the bound 1(c) hold at x = G_i(u) for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i. Let A_i^g be the set of u ∈ A_i at which these three statements and the piece_tangent statement all hold; λ(A_i ∖ A_i^g) = 0.
   Let u ∈ A_i^g and x := G_i(u). M has approximate tangent spaces range DG_i(u) and Q_x at x, so Q_x = range DG_i(u) (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Since e is a basis of ℝⁿ, range DG_i(u) = span(range v^{G_i}(u)). So for u ∈ A_i^g, ξ(G_i(u)) is a unit orientation of span(range v^{G_i}(u)).
5. (Sign, B2′.) For u ∈ A_i, v^{G_i}(u) is linearly independent, since DG_i(u) is injective and e is a basis. Apply the sibling span_orientation to v^{G_i}(u). It gives J_{G_i}(u) > 0 and ξ with α(v) = J·ξ(α), i.e. ξ = J^{-1}·ev_v. So ξ_u := J_{G_i}(u)^{-1}·ev_{v^{G_i}(u)} is a unit orientation of span(range v^{G_i}(u)), and every unit orientation of that span is ξ_u or −ξ_u.

The map u ↦ J_{G_i}(u)^{-1}·ev_{v^{G_i}(u)} is Borel: u ↦ DG_i(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv), and z ↦ ev_z and the Gram determinant are continuous. The set where two measurable maps into the finite-dimensional normed space Λ_n(ℝ^N) agree is measurable.
   By step 3, ξ'(G_i(u)) = ξ(G_i(u)) for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i. For such u ∈ A_i^g, step 4 and the uniqueness part of span_orientation give ξ(G_i(u)) ∈ {ξ_u, −ξ_u}, hence ξ(G_i(u)) = s_i(u)·ξ_u. That is:
   (★) J_{G_i}(u)·ξ(G_i(u))(α) = s_i(u)·α(v^{G_i}(u)) for every n-covector α, for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i.
6. (Weights.) Define w_i(u) := θ(G_i(u))·s_i(u) ∈ ℤ and c_i(u) := J_{G_i}(u). w_i is measurable, because θ is Borel and ℕ-valued, G_i is continuous and s_i is Borel. Moreover |w_i(u)| = θ(G_i(u)) for every u. c_i is Borel measurable: this is part (i) of the sibling area_lintegral (codim1_lura_gram_area_formula with f := G_i), whose Jacobian is exactly J_{G_i}. (Alternatively: u ↦ DG_i(u) is Borel by measurable_fderiv, and the Gram determinant and the square root are continuous.)
7. (Pointwise bound.) Let u ∈ A_i and let α be an n-covector. c_i(u) ≥ 0. By span_orientation, α(v^{G_i}(u)) = J_{G_i}(u)·ξ_u(α), and ξ_u is a unit orientation: ξ_u(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal τ. So |ξ_u(α)| ≤ |α| by (L3). Hence |α(DG_i(u)e_0, …, DG_i(u)e_{n−1})| ≤ c_i(u)·|α|.
8. (Area formulas.) For each i: A_i is Borel; G_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of A_i; and G_i is injective on A_i.
   - The sibling area_lintegral (codim1_lura_gram_area_formula with m := n, P := N, f := G_i, s := A_i) gives ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} g dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(J_{G_i}(u))·g(G_i(u)) dλ(u) for every g ≥ 0.
   - The sibling area_integral (codim1_lur_cd_injective_area_formula_gram with G := G_i, F := A_i) gives ∫_{G_i(A_i)} h dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} J_{G_i}(u)·h(G_i(u)) dλ(u) for every h : ℝ^N → ℝ.
9. (Mass bound.) By step 6 and step 8 with g := θ: ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|·c_i) dλ = ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(J_{G_i})·θ∘G_i dλ = ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ. The G_i(A_i) are pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of M. Hence Σ_i ∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{⋃_i G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_M θ dHⁿ = X.mass (lintegral_iUnion, monotonicity, 1(a)).
10. (Integrability.) By step 3, for Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N, λ(A_i ∩ G_i^{-1}(B)) ≤ m_i^{-n}·Hⁿ(G_i(A_i) ∩ B). So the image of λ⌞A_i under G_i is at most m_i^{-n}·Hⁿ⌞G_i(A_i) as measures. Using lintegral_map (θ is Borel, G_i continuous) and step 9:
    ∫⁻_{A_i} |w_i| dλ = ∫⁻_{A_i} θ∘G_i dλ = ∫⁻ θ d(G_i)_*(λ⌞A_i) ≤ m_i^{-n}·∫⁻_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ ≤ m_i^{-n}·X.mass < ∞.
    As w_i is measurable, u ↦ (w_i(u) : ℝ) is integrable on A_i.
11. (Representation.) Let η be a test form and f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(η(x)).
    - f is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M. By 1(c), |f| ≤ ‖η‖_∞·θ Hⁿ⌞M-a.e., and ∫_M θ dHⁿ < ∞ by 1(a). So f is integrable on M, and X(η) = R'.action(η) = ∫_M f dHⁿ.
    - Since Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0 and the G_i(A_i) ⊆ M are pairwise disjoint and Borel, ∫_M f dHⁿ = ∫_{⋃_i G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ. Mathlib hasSum_integral_iUnion then gives HasSum (i ↦ ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ) (X(η)).
    - For each i, step 8 (area_integral with h := f) gives ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} J_{G_i}(u)·θ(G_i(u))·ξ(G_i(u))(η(G_i(u))) dλ(u).
    - By (★) with α := η(G_i(u)), this integrand equals θ(G_i(u))·s_i(u)·η(G_i(u))(v^{G_i}(u)) = w_i(u)·η(G_i(u))(DG_i(u)e_0, …, DG_i(u)e_{n−1}) for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_i.
    Hence ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η(G_i(u))(DG_i(u)e) dλ(u) (setIntegral_congr_ae), and HasSum (i ↦ ∫_{A_i} w_i·η(G_i)(DG_i e) dλ) (X(η)).
12. Steps 2, 6 (including the measurability of w_i and c_i), 7, 9, 10 and 11 give every conclusion of the statement for these G_i, A_i, w_i and c_i. ∎

subproblems.title: Weak continuity of Jacobian minors under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants (supplied step 6(v))
subproblems.statement: Let m, p, r ∈ ℕ, L ≥ 0, and let v_j, v₀ : ℝ^m → ℝ^p (j ∈ ℕ) be L-Lipschitz maps with v_j → v₀ uniformly on ℝ^m. Let a : Fin r → Fin p (rows) and b : Fin r → Fin m (columns), and let c ∈ L¹(ℝ^m) (Lebesgue). For a map v put M^{a,b}(v)(u) := det((Dv(u)e_{b(t)})_{a(s)})_{s,t ∈ Fin r}, where Dv(u) := fderiv ℝ v u (the zero map where v is not differentiable) and e_t is the standard basis of ℝ^m. Then ∫ c·M^{a,b}(v_j) dλ → ∫ c·M^{a,b}(v₀) dλ as j → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m p r : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (v : ℕ → Euclid m → Euclid p) (v₀ : Euclid m → Euclid p) (a : Fin r → Fin p) (b : Fin r → Fin m) (c : Euclid m → ℝ), (∀ j, LipschitzWith L (v j)) → LipschitzWith L v₀ → TendstoUniformly v v₀ atTop → Integrable c → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ u, c u * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ (v j) u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ u, c u * Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun s t => fderiv ℝ v₀ u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6(v) of the supplied proof, the induction (P_r) with integration by parts for Lipschitz functions and mollification. It is written here with r×r minors of the Jacobian matrix instead of wedge products. The coefficients of β ∧ dv^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r} are signed sums of such minors, and the Piola identity of step 4 below is d(dv^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_q}) = 0 in coordinates. This is the classical weak continuity of minors (null Lagrangians) under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants (Reshetnyak; Ball 1977), which Simon uses implicitly in Ch. 6, 2.29.

Notation. λ := volume on ℝ^m = Euclid m, and ∫ means ∫ dλ over ℝ^m. e_t := EuclideanSpace.single t 1. Let v : ℝ^m → ℝ^p be L-Lipschitz.
- D_t v^i(u) := (fderiv ℝ v u (e_t))_i is the i-th coordinate (Lean: the coercion of EuclideanSpace to functions). It is defined for every u and equals the classical partial derivative where v is differentiable, i.e. λ-a.e. (Rademacher, LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt). It is Borel in u (measurable_fderiv), and |D_t v^i(u)| ≤ ‖fderiv ℝ v u‖ ≤ L everywhere (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
- For rows a : Fin r → Fin p and columns b : Fin r → Fin m, M^{a,b}(v)(u) := det(D_{b_t}v^{a_s}(u))_{s,t ∈ Fin r}. This is exactly the determinant in the statement.
- By the Leibniz formula, |M^{a,b}(v)| ≤ K_r := r!·L^r everywhere.
- The claim is: for c ∈ L¹(ℝ^m), ∫ c·M^{a,b}(v_j) → ∫ c·M^{a,b}(v₀).

1. (Integrability.) M^{a,b}(v) is Borel and bounded by K_r, so c·M^{a,b}(v) is integrable for every c ∈ L¹. All integrals below exist.
2. (Reduction to smooth compactly supported weights.) Fix r, a, b, the v_j and v₀. Suppose the claim holds for every c ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^m). Let c ∈ L¹ and ε > 0.
   - Choose a continuous compactly supported c₁ with ‖c − c₁‖_{L¹} ≤ ε (MeasureTheory.Integrable.exists_hasCompactSupport_integral_sub_le).
   - Choose φ ∈ C_c^∞ with ‖c₁ − φ‖_{L¹} ≤ ε. For example φ := c₁ ∗ ρ_δ for a mollifier ρ_δ: then φ → c₁ uniformly with supports in a fixed compact set (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
   - Then |∫ c M^{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ c M^{a,b}(v₀)| ≤ |∫ φ M^{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ φ M^{a,b}(v₀)| + 4K_r ε.
   So the lim sup is ≤ 4K_r ε for every ε > 0, and the claim holds for c.
3. (Laplace expansion.) Let r ≥ 1. Expanding along row 0 (Matrix.det_succ_row_zero):
   M^{a,b}(v) = Σ_{t ∈ Fin r} (−1)^t·D_{b_t}v^{a_0}·M_t(v),   (1)
   where M_t(v) := M^{a∘succ, b∘succAbove t}(v). This is the (r−1)×(r−1) minor with rows a_1, …, a_{r−1} and the columns of b other than b_t, in their order.
4. (Piola identity for C² maps.) Let v ∈ C²(ℝ^m; ℝ^p), q ≥ 0, a' : Fin q → Fin p and β : Fin (q+1) → Fin m. Then
   Σ_{t ∈ Fin (q+1)} (−1)^t·D_{β_t}[M^{a', β∘succAbove t}(v)] = 0 everywhere.   (2)
   For q = 0 every M^{a',·} is the 0×0 determinant 1, whose derivatives vanish. Let q ≥ 1.
   - Write N_t for the q×q matrix (D_{β_{succAbove t (t'')}}v^{a'_s})_{s,t''}.
   - The derivative of a determinant is the sum over rows of the determinants with that row differentiated. So D_{β_t} det N_t = Σ_s det N_t^{(s)}, where N_t^{(s)} is N_t with row s replaced by (D_{β_t}D_{β_{succAbove t (t'')}}v^{a'_s})_{t''}.
   - Fix s and expand det N_t^{(s)} along row s: det N_t^{(s)} = Σ_{t'≠t} (−1)^{s+π_t(t')}·D_{β_t}D_{β_{t'}}v^{a'_s}·C_s({t,t'}). Here π_t(t') := t' if t' < t and t' − 1 if t' > t is the position of column t' among the columns ≠ t. And C_s({t,t'}) is the (q−1)×(q−1) minor with rows a'_{s'} (s' ≠ s) and the columns β_{t''} with t'' ∉ {t, t'}, in order. It depends only on the unordered pair {t, t'}.
   - Hence Σ_t (−1)^t det N_t^{(s)} = Σ_{t≠t'} (−1)^{t+s+π_t(t')}·D_{β_t}D_{β_{t'}}v^{a'_s}·C_s({t,t'}).
   - For t < t' the sign of the term (t, t') is (−1)^{t+s+t'−1}, and the sign of the term (t', t) is (−1)^{t'+s+t}. These are opposite. Since v ∈ C², D_{β_t}D_{β_{t'}}v = D_{β_{t'}}D_{β_t}v (symmetry of second derivatives, ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt). So the two terms cancel and the sum is 0.
   Summing over s gives (2). (Equivalently, d(dv^{a'_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a'_q}) = 0.)
5. (Integration by parts, smooth maps.) Let v ∈ C^∞(ℝ^m; ℝ^p), φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^m) and r ≥ 1. Then
   ∫ φ·M^{a,b}(v) = −Σ_t (−1)^t ∫ D_{b_t}φ·v^{a_0}·M_t(v).   (3)
   - By (1), φM^{a,b}(v) = Σ_t (−1)^t φ·D_{b_t}v^{a_0}·M_t(v).
   - For each t, F_t := φ·v^{a_0}·M_t(v) is C¹ with compact support. By the product rule, D_{b_t}F_t = D_{b_t}φ·v^{a_0}·M_t(v) + φ·D_{b_t}v^{a_0}·M_t(v) + φ·v^{a_0}·D_{b_t}M_t(v).
   - ∫ D_{b_t}F_t = 0. Indeed, ∫ D_{b_t}F_t = lim_{h→0} ∫ (F_t(u + h e_{b_t}) − F_t(u))/h du. The difference quotients converge uniformly with supports in a fixed compact set, and ∫ F_t(u + h e_{b_t}) du = ∫ F_t du by translation invariance of λ. (Or use Mathlib integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable.)
   - Summing with signs (−1)^t, the last terms add up to −∫ φ v^{a_0} Σ_t (−1)^t D_{b_t}M_t(v). This vanishes by (2), applied with q := r − 1, a' := a∘succ, β := b. This gives (3).
6. (Integration by parts, Lipschitz maps.) (3) holds for every L-Lipschitz v : ℝ^m → ℝ^p, with all derivatives taken from fderiv as in the Notation.
   Let ρ be a standard mollifier and ρ_δ(z) := δ^{-m}ρ(z/δ) for δ > 0 (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = δ/2, rOut = δ, normed). Put v_δ := v ∗ ρ_δ, componentwise. Then:
   (i) v_δ is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left).
   (ii) v_δ is L-Lipschitz, since |v_δ(x) − v_δ(y)| ≤ ∫ ρ_δ(z)|v(x−z) − v(y−z)| dz ≤ L|x − y|. Hence |D_t v_δ^i| ≤ L.
   (iii) |v_δ − v| ≤ Lδ everywhere, so v_δ → v uniformly as δ → 0.
   (iv) D_t v_δ^i = (D_t v^i) ∗ ρ_δ. Differentiating under the integral, D_t v_δ^i(x) = ∫ D_tρ_δ(x − y) v^i(y) dy. The a.e. derivative of the Lipschitz function v^i is its weak derivative (Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq, applied with the compactly supported Lipschitz test function y ↦ ρ_δ(x − y)). This turns the right side into ∫ ρ_δ(x − y) D_t v^i(y) dy.
   (v) Along δ_ℓ := 1/(ℓ+1), D_t v_{δ_ℓ}^i → D_t v^i λ-a.e. (Lebesgue differentiation for the bounded, hence locally integrable, D_t v^i; Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable, the ratio rOut/rIn = 2 being bounded).
   Determinants are polynomial in the entries. So M^{a,b}(v_{δ_ℓ}) → M^{a,b}(v) and M_t(v_{δ_ℓ}) → M_t(v) λ-a.e., with the uniform bounds K_r, K_{r−1}; and v_{δ_ℓ}^{a_0} → v^{a_0} uniformly. Apply (3) to v_{δ_ℓ} (step 5). Both sides converge by dominated convergence: all integrands vanish outside the compact set spt φ and are uniformly bounded there, by sup|φ|·K_r and sup|Dφ|·(sup_{spt φ}|v^{a_0}| + L)·K_{r−1}. This gives (3) for v.
7. (Induction on r.) Let P(r) be the claim of the statement for all a, b, L, v_j, v₀ and c with the given r.
   - P(0) holds: M^{a,b}(v) is the 0×0 determinant 1 for every v, so both sides equal ∫ c.
   - Let r ≥ 1 and assume P(r − 1). By step 2 it suffices to treat c = φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^m). By step 6 for v_j and v₀,
     ∫ φM^{a,b}(v_j) − ∫ φM^{a,b}(v₀) = −Σ_t (−1)^t [T1_{j,t} + T2_{j,t}],
     with T1_{j,t} := ∫ D_{b_t}φ·(v_j^{a_0} − v₀^{a_0})·M_t(v_j) and T2_{j,t} := ∫ D_{b_t}φ·v₀^{a_0}·(M_t(v_j) − M_t(v₀)).
   - |T1_{j,t}| ≤ ‖D_{b_t}φ‖_{L¹}·sup_u|v_j(u) − v₀(u)|·K_{r−1} → 0, by uniform convergence (|v_j^{a_0} − v₀^{a_0}| ≤ ‖v_j − v₀‖).
   - T2_{j,t} → 0 by P(r − 1), applied with rows a∘succ, columns b∘succAbove t and weight c' := D_{b_t}φ·v₀^{a_0}. This weight is continuous with compact support, hence integrable.
   Hence ∫ φM^{a,b}(v_j) → ∫ φM^{a,b}(v₀), which proves P(r).
   By induction P(r) holds for every r, which is the statement. The cases where a or b is not injective are included: the minors then vanish identically. ∎
proof_key_steps: Minors of L-Lipschitz maps are Borel and bounded by r!L^r, so it suffices to treat weights c ∈ C_c^∞.
Laplace expansion along the first row: M^{a,b} = Σ_t (−1)^t·D_{b_t}v^{a_0}·M_t, where M_t is the (r−1)-minor without column b_t.
Piola identity Σ_t (−1)^t D_{b_t}M_t(v) = 0 for C² maps: symmetric second derivatives cancel in pairs.
Integration by parts ∫ φM^{a,b}(v) = −Σ_t (−1)^t ∫ D_{b_t}φ·v^{a_0}·M_t(v), first for smooth v, then for Lipschitz v by mollification (D(v∗ρ_δ) = Dv∗ρ_δ → Dv a.e.) and dominated convergence.
Induction on r: uniform convergence controls v_j^{a_0} − v₀^{a_0}; the induction hypothesis with weight D_{b_t}φ·v₀^{a_0} controls M_t(v_j) − M_t(v₀).

Source: step 6 (B4), parts (i)–(iv), of the supplied proof: weak continuity of pull-backs. The L¹-approximation of (ii) is not needed here, because the sibling minor_continuity already accepts L¹ weights. Simon Ch. 6, 2.29 and 3.6 use this when identifying the Lipschitz push-forward with the area-formula current.

Notation. λ := volume on ℝ^m. e_t := EuclideanSpace.single t 1 ∈ ℝ^m and e'_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^{N'}. 𝒥 is the finite set of strictly increasing maps J : Fin m → Fin N'.
- For J ∈ 𝒥 and y ∈ ℝ^{N'}, ω_J(y) := ω(y)(e'_{J(0)}, …, e'_{J(m−1)}). ω_J is continuous with compact support, being the evaluation of the continuous, compactly supported ω at a fixed family.
- For a map H : ℝ^m → ℝ^{N'} and u ∈ ℝ^m, M_J(H)(u) := det((DH(u)e_t)_{J(s)})_{s,t ∈ Fin m} with DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u. In the notation of minor_continuity this is the minor with r := m, rows a := J and columns b := id.
- ‖·‖_op is the operator norm of continuous alternating maps.

1. (Coordinate expansion.) For every m-covector α on ℝ^{N'} and every z : Fin m → ℝ^{N'},
   α(z) = Σ_{J ∈ 𝒥} α(e'_{J(0)}, …, e'_{J(m−1)})·det((z_t)_{J(s)})_{s,t}.   (E)
   Write z_t = Σ_i (z_t)_i e'_i. By multilinearity, α(z) = Σ_{f : Fin m → Fin N'} (∏_t (z_t)_{f(t)})·α(e'_{f(0)}, …, e'_{f(m−1)}).
   - If f is not injective, the family e'∘f has a repetition and the term vanishes (alternation).
   - An injective f factors uniquely as f = J∘π, with J ∈ 𝒥 the increasing enumeration of its image and π a permutation of Fin m. Then α(e'∘J∘π) = sign(π)·α(e'∘J).
   Grouping by J gives α(z) = Σ_J α(e'∘J)·Σ_π sign(π)∏_t (z_t)_{J(π(t))}, and the inner sum is det((z_t)_{J(s)})_{s,t} (Leibniz formula). (Only the scalar identity (E) is used; no coordinate covectors need to be constructed.)
   Applying (E) with α := ω(H(u)) and z := (DH(u)e_t)_t gives, for every map H and every u,
   ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{m−1}) = Σ_{J ∈ 𝒥} ω_J(H(u))·M_J(H)(u).   (E')
2. (Bounds and measurability.) Each H_j and H₀ is L-Lipschitz, so ‖DH_j(u)‖ ≤ L and ‖DH₀(u)‖ ≤ L for every u (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz). Hence every entry of the matrices in M_J is bounded by L, and |M_J(H_j)|, |M_J(H₀)| ≤ K := m!·L^m. Let C_J := sup|ω_J| < ∞.
   The functions u ↦ ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e) and the terms of (E') are Borel: u ↦ DH_j(u) is Borel (measurable_fderiv), H_j is continuous, and ω and evaluation are continuous. All integrands below are dominated by |w|·Σ_J C_J·K, which is integrable. So all integrals exist and, by (E'), ∫ w·ω(H)(DH e) = Σ_J ∫ w·(ω_J∘H)·M_J(H) for H ∈ {H_j, H₀}.
   It therefore suffices to prove, for each fixed J ∈ 𝒥, that ∫ w·(ω_J∘H_j)·M_J(H_j) → ∫ w·(ω_J∘H₀)·M_J(H₀).
3. (Two terms.) Write the difference as T1_j + T2_j, where
   T1_j := ∫ w·(ω_J∘H_j − ω_J∘H₀)·M_J(H_j) and T2_j := ∫ w·(ω_J∘H₀)·(M_J(H_j) − M_J(H₀)).
   (a) T1_j → 0. ω_J is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support) and H_j → H₀ uniformly. So δ_j := sup_u |ω_J(H_j(u)) − ω_J(H₀(u))| → 0, and |T1_j| ≤ δ_j·K·‖w‖_{L¹} → 0.
   (b) T2_j → 0. Apply the sibling minor_continuity with m, p := N', r := m, the same L, v := (H_j)_j, v₀ := H₀, rows a := J, columns b := id and weight c := w·(ω_J∘H₀). The weight is measurable and |c| ≤ C_J|w|, so c is integrable. The sibling gives ∫ c·M_J(H_j) → ∫ c·M_J(H₀), i.e. T2_j → 0. (Its matrix entry fderiv ℝ (v j) u (EuclideanSpace.single (b t) 1) (a s) is (DH_j(u)e_t)_{J(s)}.)
4. Summing over the finitely many J ∈ 𝒥 gives ∫ w(u)·ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e) du → ∫ w(u)·ω(H₀(u))(DH₀(u)e) du. For m = 0 the argument still applies: 𝒥 has one element (the empty map), every determinant equals 1, and T2_j = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinate expansion: α(z) = Σ_J α(e'_J)·det((z_t)_{J(s)}) over strictly increasing J, by multilinearity, alternation and the Leibniz formula.
Hence ω(H u)(DH(u)e) = Σ_J ω_J(H u)·M_J(H)(u), with |M_J| ≤ m!L^m and ω_J continuous with compact support.
For each J, the term with ω_J(H_j) − ω_J(H₀) tends to 0 by uniform continuity of ω_J and uniform convergence of H_j.
The remaining term tends to 0 by minor_continuity with the L¹ weight w·ω_J(H₀).

subproblems.title: The Lipschitz image of an integer-weighted Lebesgue piece is an integer multiplicity current (supplied step 5, B3; Simon 6.3.5–3.9)

(IMSc) says: for all P, k and W : ℕ → 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with Σ_l M(W_l) < ∞ there is S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^P) with S(ω) = Σ_l W_l(ω) (HasSum) for every ω, M(S) ≤ Σ_l M(W_l) and spt S ⊆ closure ⋃_l spt W_l, and S is integer multiplicity if every W_l is. Let N', k ∈ ℕ, n := k + 1, L ≥ 0, let H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'} be L-Lipschitz, A ⊆ ℝⁿ Borel, and g : ℝⁿ → ℤ measurable with ∫_A |g| dλ < ∞. subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 (B3) of the supplied proof, stated for one Lipschitz map H with an integer weight g. Its ingredients are the bi-Lipschitz pieces A_{il}, the images N_{il} with integer densities and induced orientations η_{il}, the integer multiplicity currents Φ_{il} with their mass bound, and their combination by IMS. This is Simon Ch. 6, 3.5–3.9: f_#τ(M, θ, ξ) is integer multiplicity, with the induced orientation d f_# ξ/|d f_# ξ| on f(M_+).

Hypotheses as named in the statement:
- (CB): its third conjunct (L3) says |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ.
- (IMC): only part (b) is used.
- (IMSc) is the conclusion of the frozen type of cmcdt_im_series. For every sequence W_l ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}) with Σ_l M(W_l) < ∞ there is S with HasSum (l ↦ W_l(ω)) (S(ω)) for every ω, M(S) ≤ Σ_l M(W_l) and spt S ⊆ closure ⋃_l spt W_l; and S is integer multiplicity if every W_l is.

Notation:
- n := k + 1; λ := volume on ℝⁿ; Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^{N'}; e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α.
- DH(u) := fderiv ℝ H u (0 where H is not differentiable); v(u) := (DH(u)e_a)_{a ∈ Fin n}; J(u) := √det(⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩)_{a,b}.
- ev_z := (α ↦ α(z)) ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^{N'}); for a test form ω, Ψ_ω(u) := g(u)·ω(H(u))(v(u)).

1. (Integrability.) ‖DH(u)‖ ≤ L for all u (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz), so |DH(u)e_a| ≤ L. Also |ω(y)(z)| ≤ ‖ω(y)‖·∏_a|z_a|, with C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ because ω is continuous with compact support. Ψ_ω is Borel: g is measurable, H continuous, u ↦ DH(u) Borel (measurable_fderiv) and evaluation continuous. Since |Ψ_ω| ≤ C_ω·Lⁿ·|g|, Ψ_ω is integrable on A.
2. (Where the integrand lives.)
   - D := {u : H is differentiable at u} is Borel (measurableSet_of_differentiableAt), and λ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0 (Rademacher, LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt).
   - A⁺ := {u ∈ A ∩ D : DH(u) injective and g(u) ≠ 0} is Borel: DH(u) is injective iff det(⟨DH(u)e_a, DH(u)e_b⟩) ≠ 0, a Borel condition.
   - Let u ∈ (A ∩ D) ∖ A⁺. Either g(u) = 0, or DH(u) is not injective, so v(u) is linearly dependent and ω(H(u))(v(u)) = 0 (an alternating map vanishes on linearly dependent families, AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent). In both cases Ψ_ω(u) = 0.
   Hence Ψ_ω = 0 λ-a.e. on A ∖ A⁺, and ∫_A Ψ_ω dλ = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω dλ. Moreover λ(A⁺) ≤ ∫⁻_A |g| dλ < ∞, since |g| ≥ 1 on A⁺.
3. (Bi-Lipschitz partition.) For a linear map T : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'}: if T is injective, choose κ_T > 0 with |Tw| ≥ κ_T|w| for all w (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith, κ_T := 1/K) and put r(T) := κ_T/2; otherwise put r(T) := 1. Then r(T) ≠ 0 for every T.
   Apply Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt to f := H, s := A⁺, f' := DH and this r. (At u ∈ A⁺, H is differentiable, so HasFDerivWithinAt H (DH u) A⁺ u.) It gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with A⁺ ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear maps T_l such that |H(u) − H(u') − T_l(u − u')| ≤ r(T_l)|u − u'| for u, u' ∈ A_l := A⁺ ∩ t_l. If A⁺ ≠ ∅, then T_l = DH(y_l) for some y_l ∈ A⁺, so T_l is injective.
   Then for u, u' ∈ A_l: |H(u) − H(u')| ≥ |T_l(u − u')| − (κ_{T_l}/2)|u − u'| ≥ κ_l|u − u'|, with κ_l := κ_{T_l}/2 > 0. (If A⁺ = ∅, every A_l is empty; take κ_l := 1.)
   The A_l are Borel and pairwise disjoint, with ⋃_l A_l = A⁺. H is injective on each A_l, and differentiable with injective derivative at every point of A_l.
4. (Jacobian facts.) For u ∈ A⁺, v(u) is linearly independent. By the sibling span_orientation: J(u) > 0; J(u) ≤ ∏_a |DH(u)e_a| ≤ Lⁿ; and ξ_u := J(u)^{-1}·ev_{v(u)} is a unit orientation of span(range v(u)) = range DH(u). (The sibling's ξ satisfies α(v) = J·ξ(α), so ξ = J^{-1}·ev_v.)
5. (One piece.) Fix l.
   - N_l := H(A_l) is Borel (Lusin–Souslin: H is continuous and injective on the Borel set A_l; MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn).
   - Let h_l : ℝ^{N'} → ℝⁿ satisfy h_l(H(u)) = u for u ∈ A_l (an inverse on N_l, arbitrary elsewhere, e.g. Function.invFunOn). For Borel B ⊆ ℝⁿ, N_l ∩ h_l^{-1}(B) = H(A_l ∩ B) is Borel, so h_l is Borel on N_l.
   - m_l(y) := g(h_l(y)) for y ∈ N_l and m_l(y) := 0 otherwise. It is integer-valued and measurable.
   - η_l(y) := ξ_{h_l(y)} = J(h_l(y))^{-1}·ev_{v(h_l(y))} for y ∈ N_l and η_l(y) := 0 otherwise. It is Borel into the finite-dimensional space Λ_n(ℝ^{N'}), hence strongly measurable.
   Check the hypotheses of the sibling int_density_imrep (cmcdt_ims_imrep_of_int_density with P := N', U := ℝ^{N'}, N := N_l, η := η_l, m := m_l):
   - ℝ^{N'} is open, and N_l is a Borel subset of it.
   - N_l ⊆ range H with H Lipschitz, so N_l is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range and CountablyRectifiable.mono).
   - By the sibling area_lintegral (f := H, s := A_l; H is differentiable with injective derivative and injective on A_l): Hⁿ(N_l) = ∫⁻_{A_l} ofReal(J) dλ ≤ Lⁿ·λ(A_l) ≤ Lⁿ·λ(A⁺) < ∞. So Hⁿ(N_l ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K.
   - Since m_l(H(u)) = g(u) for u ∈ A_l, area_lintegral with the weight |m_l| gives ∫⁻_{N_l ∩ K} |m_l| dHⁿ ≤ ∫⁻_{N_l} |m_l| dHⁿ = ∫⁻_{A_l} ofReal(J)·|g| dλ ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_{A_l} |g| dλ < ∞.
   - Orientation. By the sibling piece_tangent (ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae with F := H, B := A_l, L, m := κ_l), for λ-a.e. u ∈ A_l, N_l has approximate tangent space range DH(u) at H(u); and η_l(H(u)) = ξ_u is a unit orientation of range DH(u) (step 4). Let E ⊆ A_l be the λ-null exceptional set and E' ⊇ E a Borel λ-null subset of A_l. By area_lintegral, Hⁿ(H(E')) = ∫⁻_{E'} ofReal(J) dλ = 0. Every y ∈ N_l ∖ H(E') is H(u) with u ∈ A_l ∖ E. Hence for Hⁿ⌞N_l-a.e. y there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n N_l y Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (η_l y) Q.
   So int_density_imrep gives an IMRep R_l in ℝ^{N'} with R_l.action(ω) = ∫_{N_l} m_l·η_l(ω) dHⁿ for every form ω.
   By (IMC)(b) with U := E := ℝ^{N'}, there are a current Φ_l and an IMRep R'_l representing Φ_l, with carrier R_l.carrier ∩ ℝ^{N'} = R_l.carrier and with the multiplicity and orientation of R_l. Hence R'_l.action = R_l.action, Φ_l is integer multiplicity, and Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{N_l} m_l·η_l(ω) dHⁿ for every test form ω.
6. (Formula for Φ_l.) Let ω be a test form. The sibling area_integral (G := H, F := A_l, h(y) := m_l(y)·η_l(y)(ω(y))) gives ∫_{N_l} m_l·η_l(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{A_l} J(u)·g(u)·J(u)^{-1}·ω(H(u))(v(u)) dλ(u) = ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω dλ, since J > 0 on A_l. So Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω dλ.
7. (Mass of Φ_l.) Let ω be admissible for Φ_l.mass = Φ_l.massOn ℝ^{N'}, i.e. a test form with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ N_l, η_l(y) is a unit orientation: η_l(y)(α) = ±α(τ) with τ orthonormal. So |η_l(y)(ω(y))| ≤ |ω(y)| ≤ 1 by (L3). Hence Φ_l(ω) ≤ ∫_{N_l} |m_l| dHⁿ ≤ Lⁿ·∫_{A_l} |g| dλ (step 5), and Φ_l.mass = sSup{ofReal(Φ_l(ω)) : ω admissible} ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞)ⁿ·∫⁻_{A_l} |g| dλ.
8. (Summation.) By lintegral_iUnion over the disjoint Borel sets A_l, Σ_l Φ_l.mass ≤ Lⁿ·Σ_l ∫⁻_{A_l} |g| dλ = Lⁿ·∫⁻_{A⁺} |g| dλ ≤ Lⁿ·∫⁻_A |g| dλ < ∞.
   Apply (IMSc) (with P := N' and this k) to W := (Φ_l)_{l ∈ ℕ}. It gives S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{N'}) with HasSum (l ↦ Φ_l(ω)) (S(ω)) for every test form ω; S is integer multiplicity because every Φ_l is.
   For a test form ω, Ψ_ω is integrable on A⁺ = ⋃_l A_l (disjoint Borel sets), so HasSum (l ↦ ∫_{A_l} Ψ_ω dλ) (∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω dλ) (hasSum_integral_iUnion). By step 6 and uniqueness of sums, S(ω) = ∫_{A⁺} Ψ_ω dλ = ∫_A Ψ_ω dλ (step 2) = ∫_A g(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_0, …, DH(u)e_{n−1}) dλ(u). ∎
proof_key_steps: Rademacher and alternation: the integrand vanishes a.e. off A⁺ = A ∩ {DH injective} ∩ {g ≠ 0}, and λ(A⁺) ≤ ∫_A|g| < ∞.
Mathlib's approximately-linear partition, with r(T) half the coercivity constant of T, splits A⁺ into disjoint Borel pieces A_l on which H is bi-Lipschitz.
On N_l = H(A_l), take the integer density m_l = g∘H⁻¹ and the orientation η_l = J⁻¹·(α ↦ α(DH e))∘H⁻¹; piece_tangent and span_orientation show that η_l orients N_l a.e.
int_density_imrep and (IMC)(b) give an integer multiplicity current Φ_l. area_integral gives Φ_l(ω) = ∫_{A_l} g·ω(H)(DH e), and (L3) with area_lintegral gives M(Φ_l) ≤ Lⁿ∫_{A_l}|g|.
IMS sums the Φ_l, and countable additivity identifies the sum with ∫_A g·ω(H)(DH e).

subproblems.title: Integrality (I): the limit of smooth push-forwards of an integer multiplicity current is integer multiplicity (supplied step 7)
subproblems.statement: Assume, as hypotheses, (CB) the frozen type of Submission.cmcdt_lp_covector_norm_bounds, and (VO), (MR), (IMC), (IMS) exactly as in the selected statement (the frozen types of dtc_vanish_off_support, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub and cmcdt_im_series, as antecedents). Then conclusion (I) of the selected statement holds. Let N, N', k ∈ ℕ, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} Λ-Lipschitz, X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) integer multiplicity with compact support and M(X) < ∞, and S ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}). Suppose there are C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) Λ-Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} converging to F uniformly on ℝ^N such that, for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}), there are test forms η_j ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^N), each equal to F_j^#ω (x ↦ ω(F_j(x)) ∘ DF_j(x)) on some open set containing spt X, with X(η_j) → S(ω). Then S is integer multiplicity.

Source: step 7 of the supplied proof, with the set-up of its step 4 and the IMS summation of its step 5(d). This is Simon Ch. 6, 2.29 and 3.6–3.9: the Lipschitz push-forward is the limit of the smooth push-forwards f^{(σ)}_#T and equals the integer multiplicity current given by the area formula.

Hypotheses:
- (CB), whose first conjunct (L1) says |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β| for linear A and k-covectors β (Lean: covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β);
- (VO), (MR), (IMC) and (IMS) as in the statement;
- (IMSc) denotes (IMS) applied to (VO), (MR) and (IMC).
Fix N, N', k, Λ, F, X and S as in the statement. Put n := k + 1, |·| := covectorEuclideanNorm and e_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1.

1. (Pieces.) Apply the sibling piece_representation to (CB), (VO), (MR), (IMC) and X; X is integer multiplicity with X.mass < ∞. It gives maps G_i (L_i-Lipschitz), Borel sets A_i, measurable w_i : ℝⁿ → ℤ and functions c_i such that:
   - G_i is differentiable on A_i and G_i(A_i) ⊆ spt X;
   - w_i is integrable on A_i, and w_i, c_i are measurable;
   - c_i ≥ 0 and |α(DG_i(u)e)| ≤ c_i(u)·|α| for u ∈ A_i and every n-covector α on ℝ^N;
   - Σ_i ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|c_i) ≤ X.mass;
   - HasSum (i ↦ ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e) du) (X(η)) for every test form η on ℝ^N.
   Put B_i := ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|c_i). Each B_i is finite and Σ_i B_i ≤ X.mass < ∞.
2. (Approximating maps.) Take the F_j (j ∈ ℕ) from the hypothesis: C^∞ (in particular differentiable everywhere), Λ-Lipschitz, with F_j → F uniformly. Then ‖DF_j(x)‖ ≤ Λ for all x (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
   Put H_{ij} := F_j ∘ G_i and H_i := F ∘ G_i. These maps are (Λ·L_i)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp). As j → ∞, H_{ij} → H_i uniformly on ℝⁿ (TendstoUniformly.comp).
3. (Chain rule.) For u ∈ A_i, F_j is differentiable at G_i(u) and G_i is differentiable at u, so DH_{ij}(u) = DF_j(G_i(u)) ∘ DG_i(u) (fderiv_comp). Hence for every form ω on ℝ^{N'}, ω(H_{ij}(u))(DH_{ij}(u)e) = β_{ij}(u)(DG_i(u)e), where β_{ij}(u) := ω(F_j(G_i u)).compContinuousLinearMap(DF_j(G_i u)) is an n-covector on ℝ^N.
4. (Fix ω.) Let ω be a test form on ℝ^{N'} and ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_y |ω(y)|, which is finite. Let η_j be the test forms of the hypothesis: there are open sets W_j ⊇ spt X with η_j(x) = ω(F_j(x)).compContinuousLinearMap(DF_j(x)) for x ∈ W_j, and X(η_j) → S(ω).
5. (Expansion of X(η_j).) By step 1, HasSum (i ↦ T_{ij}) (X(η_j)), where T_{ij} := ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η_j(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e) du. For u ∈ A_i we have G_i(u) ∈ spt X ⊆ W_j, so η_j(G_i u) = β_{ij}(u). By step 3, T_{ij} = ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·ω(H_{ij}(u))(DH_{ij}(u)e) du.
6. (Uniform domination.) For u ∈ A_i, using step 1 and then (L1):
   |ω(H_{ij}(u))(DH_{ij}(u)e)| = |β_{ij}(u)(DG_i(u)e)| ≤ c_i(u)·|β_{ij}(u)| ≤ c_i(u)·‖DF_j(G_i u)‖ⁿ·|ω(F_j(G_i u))| ≤ Λⁿ‖ω‖_∞·c_i(u).
   Hence |T_{ij}| ≤ ∫_{A_i} |w_i|·|ω(H_{ij})(DH_{ij}e)| ≤ b_i := Λⁿ‖ω‖_∞·B_i.toReal (lintegral_mono, lintegral_const_mul'). The bound b_i does not depend on j. Moreover Σ_i b_i ≤ Λⁿ‖ω‖_∞·X.mass.toReal < ∞, and b is summable (ENNReal.summable_toReal).
7. (Termwise limit.) Fix i. Apply the sibling pullback_continuity with m := n, N', L := Λ·L_i, H := (H_{ij})_j, H₀ := H_i, w := (indicator of A_i)·w_i (integrable by step 1) and ω (continuous with compact support). It gives ∫ 1_{A_i}w_i·ω(H_{ij})(DH_{ij}e) → ∫ 1_{A_i}w_i·ω(H_i)(DH_i e). That is, T_{ij} → T_i := ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·ω(H_i(u))(DH_i(u)e) du as j → ∞ (integral_indicator).
8. (Identification.) By Tannery's theorem (tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence) with steps 6 and 7, Σ_i T_{ij} → Σ_i T_i as j → ∞. By step 5, Σ_i T_{ij} = X(η_j) → S(ω). Hence S(ω) = Σ_i T_i(ω). Also |T_i(ω)| ≤ b_i, as a limit of terms bounded by b_i. This holds for every test form ω. (☆)
9. (Integer pieces.) For each i, apply the sibling piece_current to (CB), (IMC), (IMSc) and H := H_i (Λ·L_i-Lipschitz), A := A_i, g := w_i (measurable and integrable on A_i). It gives an integer multiplicity S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{N'}) with S_i(ω) = T_i(ω) for every test form ω.
10. (Masses.) Let ω be admissible for S_i.mass, i.e. |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. Then ‖ω‖_∞ ≤ 1, and by step 8, S_i(ω) = T_i(ω) ≤ |T_i(ω)| ≤ Λⁿ·B_i.toReal. So S_i.mass = sSup{ofReal(S_i(ω)) : ω admissible} ≤ (Λ : ℝ≥0∞)ⁿ·B_i, and Σ_i S_i.mass ≤ Λⁿ·X.mass < ∞.
11. (Sum.) Apply (IMSc) (with P := N' and this k) to W := (S_i)_i. It gives Ŝ with HasSum (i ↦ S_i(ω)) (Ŝ(ω)) for every ω, and Ŝ is integer multiplicity because every S_i is. By (☆) and step 9, Ŝ(ω) = Σ_i T_i(ω) = S(ω) for every test form ω. If R̂ is an IMRep representing Ŝ, then S(ω) = Ŝ(ω) = R̂.action(ω) for all ω. So R̂ represents S, and S is integer multiplicity. ∎

2. (Product pieces.) For each i define Ĝ_i : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{N+1} by Ĝ_i(z) := ι(z_0, G_i(tail z)), Â_i := {z : z_0 ∈ (0, 1) and tail z ∈ A_i}, and ŵ_i(z) := w_i(tail z).

In particular ∫⁻_{Â_i} |ŵ_i| = ∫⁻_{A_i} |w_i| < ∞, so ŵ_i is integrable on Â_i.

That is, (DĜ_i(z)ê_a)_{a ∈ Fin (n+1)} = Fin.cons e₀ (b ↦ J(DG_i(u)e_b)).
3. (Representation of C.) Fix a test form ω on ℝ^{N+1}, let η be the test form given by the hypothesis, and put f_{i,ω}(z) := ω(Ĝ_i z)(DĜ_i(z)ê_0, …, DĜ_i(z)ê_n).

   - ŵ_i·f_{i,ω} is measurable and bounded on Â_i by |ŵ_i|·sup_y‖ω(y)‖·max(1, L_i)^{n+1}, so it is integrable on Â_i.
   By piece_representation and 2(c):
   C(ω) = X(η) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e) du = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·∫_{(0,1)} f_{i,ω}(ι'(t, u)) dt du = Σ_i ∫_{Â_i} ŵ_i(z)·ω(Ĝ_i z)(DĜ_i(z)ê) dz,
   as a HasSum.
4. (Integer pieces.) For each i, apply the sibling piece_current to (CB), (IMC), (IMSc) with N' := N + 1, k := k + 1, H := Ĝ_i, A := Â_i and g := ŵ_i. It gives an integer multiplicity Ŝ_i ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) with Ŝ_i(ω) = ∫_{Â_i} ŵ_i(z)·ω(Ĝ_i z)(DĜ_i(z)ê) dz for every test form ω.

   Hence Ŝ_i.mass = sSup{ofReal(Ŝ_i(ω)) : ω admissible} ≤ B_i, and Σ_i Ŝ_i.mass ≤ X.mass < ∞.

By steps 3 and 4, C(ω) = Σ_i Ŝ_i(ω) = Ĉ(ω) for every test form ω. So an IMRep representing Ĉ also represents C, and C is integer multiplicity. ∎
